what: Maintainers, people or AI agents, change what the code does and know that every behavior its specification asks for still holds, as the code holds only those behaviors, and whoever runs the code can fix a wrong input from outside.

critical_success_factors.what: The maintainer finds the one place where a change belongs.

necessary_conditions.what: Does each module say, where the maintainer first meets it, the one thing it alone decides?
Does each name that a module offers state everything a caller needs to call it without reading its body?
Does each behavior of the code trace to a case of its specification, which is what was agreed for the part?

critical_success_factors.what: The tests show whether every behavior still holds.

necessary_conditions.what: Do the tests pass in any order and on every run, on a fresh machine set up from the code's setup alone?
Does each case of the specification, its edges and refusals included, have one test whose name says the case?
Do the tests call the code only as its callers do, through its interfaces?
Does each test assert the whole result of its case, with coverage leaving no line that no case calls for, and no two tests on the same branch for the same case?

critical_success_factors.what: Whoever runs the code can fix a wrong input from outside.

necessary_conditions.what: Does the code refuse a wrong input from outside before it acts, with a message from which whoever ran it can fix the input?

outcome: A user who leaves AI work running at night finds it carried through by morning, as work stopped at the usage limit or by an error resumes on its own once it can, and the next work starts when one ends.
solution: The user starts one work from Claude Code by `overnight`, with its folder, its prompt, and the tools it may use, and leaves; it runs apart from the session through `claude -p`, so closing Claude Code doesn't stop it, and on the usage limit or any error it is asked to go on in the same conversation after a wait of 5, 10, then 60 minutes, up to 7 retries by default or as many as the user says, so that by morning the work is done, or recorded as failed, with its log.
assumptions: A run succeeded exactly when `claude -p --output-format json` exits 0 and its result has `is_error` false; the usage limit and other errors show as anything else.
`claude -p --resume <session_id>` goes on from where the failed run stopped.
Asking again while the limit holds only fails again, and does no harm.
Waits of 5, 10, then 60 minutes each, 7 times, wait 5 hours and 15 minutes in all, so they outlast the 5-hour limit after any stop, and resume within an hour of its lifting.
Unit tests with a stand-in for `claude` that answers as the real one does show that it works, so the user need not try it on a real night.
